notes:
Prospect profile: mid-to-large fintech platform offering personalized investor communications. Very security-conscious; primary blocker is procurement + infosec.

Key asks heard repeatedly: VPC-only control plane, HSM/KMS integration, retention windows per-regulation, signed BAA and subprocessor list. Wants 95th percentile chat latency <350ms at sustained 50 rps for 3 concurrent models (assistant + reranker + embedder).

What happened: strong early interest, SE session went well (Priya ran token-cost estimate). Procurement instituted Q1 hiring freeze -> budget put on hold. Meanwhile internal platform team prioritized quick-win pilot and selected LegacyVendorA for an exploratory pilot (they could stand up a limited endpoint inside 2 weeks). Rivermark never committed an internal product owner to allocate infra/resource time for Redwood POC.

Sales/eng notes (fragments):
- AE/Jordan: "They liked performance numbers but can't get procurement sign-off yet."
- SE/Priya: "Security team still needs formal HSM support statement + audit log retention SLA; pushed our security FAQ on 2024-11-09."
- Procurement: "No budget till FY Q2 review; cannot sign new capacity contracts."
- Product lead (Rivermark): 'We'd prefer vendor that can do turnkey VPC demo; timeline slipped.'

Risks: prospect will fully onboard with competitor if their pilot meets minimal UX; otherwise could re-emerge post-budget with updated success criteria. POC never kicked off because no internal sponsor/resourcing.

Suggested salvage play: 1) Provide an 'air-gap friendly' canned demo with clear HSM/KMS checklist and audit screenshots; 2) Offer short-term trial credits contingent on security/contract pre-approval to reduce procurement friction; 3) Identify and re-engage a technical champion in infra (ask AE to wedge intro to platform ops).
